messages:
lina: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — thinking about 'soft caps' that slow but don't hard-evict tenants during short surges. want to brainstorm tradeoffs for fairness scheduling + abuse prevention.

sanjay: +1. main concern is noisy tenants gaming the slow path to keep throughput. if soft caps only add latency they might still dominate.

anna: we've tried a variant in staging: admission returns one of {accepted, soft_shed, reject}. soft_shed => probabilistic drop + lower priority queue. drop rate is tuned per-tenant based on recent burstiness.

mike: metric callout: we need token_burst, steady_rps, and kv_cache_hit_rate to decide whether a spike is legit. without cache signals soft_shed will penalize legitimate warm-up traffic.

jonathan: could we add a short-lived abuse_score from the fraud-detector service as an admission_hint? low-cost check (sampled) and if score>threshold bias towards reject/higher drop-rate. fallback: routing to cheaper model variants.

claire: ops note — be careful with telemetry cardinality. per-tenant-per-second signals explode. prefer minute-aggregates and a small set of derived signals we can index.

lina: agreed on aggregated telemetry. also want to discuss enforcement point: ingress (edge) vs serving nodes. edge = fast cheap decisions; serving layer can do heavier rebalancing and true lease revocation.

sanjay: proposal: two-layer control. 1) edge does lightweight probabilistic shedding + tag requests with probe flags. 2) central allocator ingests aggregates + issues ephemeral leases/weight adjustments. if tenant exceeds sustained window, escalate to hard reject or eviction.

anna: config example (pseudo):
```json
{"policy_version":"softcap-v1","soft_threshold_tokens_per_min":10000,"drop_curve":"linear","probe_sample_rate":0.01,"grace_tokens":500}
```
probe_sample_rate used to feed ML model and to validate that we aren't punishing warm-up patterns.

mike: another tradeoff: client experience. for PLG customers, small probabilistic drops are ok; enterprise SLAs need explicit canary/grace allowances and manual overrides. need a control-plane flag for emergency un-shed.

jonathan: on abuse detection: we should differentiate scripted high-rate behavior from legitimate parallel inference (many small requests). classifier features: inter-request delta, unique prompt entropy, kv_cache_hit_rate, embedding-only ratio. sample + hill-climb thresholds in prod.

claire: ops playbook: when softcap triggers, send a tenant-level alert with buckets: "soft_shed_active", "drop_rate", "trend". autosnooze if manual ack. minimize paging noise.

lina: implementation questions: 1) should softcap policy live in the ingress config (fast path) or be consulted via sidecar? 2) how do we version policies for staged rollouts?

sanjay: sidecar adds latency but centralizes logic. i'm leaning to edge config + sidecar enrichment. versioning: policy_id + rollout_fraction in config so we can canary by tenant.

anna: we also need to reserve control-plane tokens for migrations, canary tests, and on-call ops. these should be exempt from softcap or have separate grace quotas.

ops-bot: heads-up: scheduled maintenance will reduce dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 next Tue 03:00-05:00 UTC — this will interact with any softcap experiments.

lina: good catch @ops-bot — we'll avoid canarying large changes during that window.

mike: next steps: document config schema, add minimal metrics to edge (aggregated minute), and run a 1% tenant canary with probe_sample_rate=0.05 and drop_curve=gentle.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: softcap-prototype v0.1 -> staging at 6201113000.

lina: sweet. sync tomorrow 11am to agree on telemetry fields and the ML sampling pipeline. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
